==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈɹɪdəl/|[ˈɹʷɪdəl]|~|[ˈɹʷɪdl̩]}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-riddle.wav|a=Southern England}} *** {{IPA|en|/ˈɹɪɾəl/|[ˈɹʷɪɾəl]|~|[ˈɹʷɪɾl̩]|a=US,CA,t-flapping}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪdəl|s=2}} * {{hyph|en|rid|dle}} ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:redel|id=puzzle|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|redel}}, {{m|enm|redels}}, from {{inh|en|ang|rǣdels}}, {{m|ang|rǣdelse|t=counsel, opinion, imagination, riddle}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*rādislī|t=counsel, conjecture}}. Analyzable as {{af|en|rede|t1=advice|-le}}. Akin to {{cog|ang|rǣdan||to read, advise, interpret}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|raadsel}}, {{cog|de|Rätsel}}. ====Noun==== {{examples|: '''6th c. {{BCE}}''', Laozi, ''{{w|Tao Te Ching}}'' 9: :: Keep sharpening the blade, you'll soon blunt it. : {{RQ:King James Version|Luke|17|33}} :: Whosoever shall seek to save his life shall lose it; and whosoever shall lose his life shall preserve it. |sense=ancient form}} {{en-noun}} # A [[verbal]] [[puzzle]], [[mystery]], or other [[problem]] of an [[intellectual]] nature. #: {{syn|en|enigma|conundrum|brain-teaser}} #: {{ux|en|Here's a '''riddle''': It's black, and white, and red all over. What is it?}} #* {{RQ:King James Version|Judges|14|12|14|passage=12 ¶ And Samson said vnto them, I will now put foorth a '''riddle''' vnto you: if you can certeinly declare it me, within the seuen dayes of the feast, and finde it out, then I will giue you thirtie sheetes, and thirtie change of garments:
13 But if ye cannot declare it me, then shall yee giue me thirtie sheetes, and thirtie change of garments. And they said vnto him, Put foorth thy '''riddle''', that we may heare it.
14 And hee said vnto them, Out of the eater came foorth meate, aud out of the strong came foorth sweetnesse. And they could not in three dayes expound the '''riddle'''.}} #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Regained|book=Samson Agonistes|page=72|passage=To wring from me and tell to them my ſecret, / That ſolv'd the '''riddle''' which I had propos'd.}} #* {{RQ:Chambers Younger Set|VIII|passage=Elbows almost touching they leaned at ease, idly reading the almost obliterated lines engraved there. ¶ {{nowrap|"I never}} understood it," she observed, lightly scornful. "What occult meaning has a sun-dial for the spooney? ''I'm'' sure I don't want to read '''riddles''' in a strange gentleman's optics."}} #* {{quote-song|en|year=1992|artist={{w|Alice in Chains|Alice in Chains}}|title={{w|Dirt (Alice in Chains album)|Rain When I Die}}|passage=I'm a '''riddle''' so strong, you can't break me}} # An ancient verbal, poetic, or literary form, in which, rather than a [[rhyme]] scheme, there are parallel opposing expressions with a hidden meaning. =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|riddlelike|riddlesome|world riddle|riddler|riddle canon|riddle wrapped in an enigma|riddle me ree|riddle me this|riddle stick}} {{clear}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|verbal puzzle}} * Afrikaans: * Ahtna: * Albanian: * Arabic: * Armenian: * Assamese: * Azerbaijani: * Bashkir: * Belarusian: * Bhojpuri: * Bulgarian: * Burmese: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Faroese: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Indonesian: * Ingrian: * Irish: * Italian: * Ivatan: * Japanese: * Kapampangan: * Kazakh: * Korean: * Kyrgyz: * Ladino: * Latin: * Latvian: * Lithuanian: * Macedonian: * Malay: * Māori: * Middle English: * Mirandese: * Norwegian: * Occitan: * Pashto: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|зага́дка|f}}, {{t+|ru|ре́бус|m}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Serbo-Croatian: * Sicilian: * Slovak: * Slovene: * Southern Altai: * Spanish: * Sundanese: * Swahili: * Swedish: * Tagalog: * Tajik: * Thai: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: * Urdu: * Uyghur: * Uzbek: * Vietnamese: * Walloon: * Welsh: * Yakan: {{trans-bottom}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # More at {{l|en|rinse}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|sieve}} A [[sieve]] with coarse [[mesh]]es, usually of wire, for separating coarser materials from finer, as chaff from grain, cinders from ashes, or gravel from sand. # A [[board]] with a row of [[pin]]s, set [[zigzag]], between which wire is drawn to [[straighten]] it. =====Translations===== {{trans-see|sieve}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # To put something through a [[#Noun 2|riddle]] or [[sieve#Noun|sieve]]; to [[sieve#Verb|sieve]]; to [[sift#Verb|sift]]. #: {{ux|en|You have to '''riddle''' the gravel before you lay it on the road.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|author=Helen Yemm|title=Thorny problems: How can I revive a forsythia hedge? # {{lb|en|engineering}} To have rotation in such direction that the crank pin traverses the upper, or front, half of its path in the forward, or outward, stroke; said of a crank which drives, or is driven by, a reciprocating piece.

====Usage notes====
* The verb and the particle are generally inseparable, even when the object is a pronoun.
** However, in the sense of "to drive over" (a thing or person), the pair is often separated: ''He didn't see the raccoon in time to brake, and sadly he '''ran''' it '''over'''''; or, ''He didn't see the raccoon in time to brake, and sadly he '''ran over''' it''.
